findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7 — P1 confidence 100 blocking — Provider-contract collapse: when synchronization is enabled, `return response` forwards the documented access-token-and-expiry-only Fetch response unchanged to consumers that require mutually incompatible representations (Google reads Gaxios `.data`, HubSpot reads SDK camelCase fields, Lark requires a nested `data` envelope, and Webex requires refresh-token and scope literals), so synchronized refresh deterministically supplies undefined or schema-invalid token fields.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — P1 confidence 100 blocking — Origin/configuration conflation: `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` selects the generic schema for every parse while the feature is configured, including the direct Salesforce provider response, so Salesforce metadata such as `instance_url` is stripped before persistence and the next client is built from an incomplete credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — P1 confidence 100 blocking — Invalid schema shape: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` creates one literal JavaScript property rather than an arbitrary numeric-expiry field, so Zod strips real keys such as `expires_in` and `expiry_date` from synchronized responses and persisted credentials immediately lose the expiry information used to decide when to refresh.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — P1 confidence 100 blocking — Persistence-envelope drift: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` captures a Zod `safeParse` result and stores that `{ success, data }` wrapper as the credential key, so every Google refresh corrupts the database shape and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` rejects it.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — P1 confidence 100 blocking — Sentinel semantic collapse: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` stores a placeholder that satisfies string schemas and overwrites Office 365's usable local refresh token after a synchronized refresh, so disabling or losing the sync endpoint routes the provider fallback with the literal sentinel and makes the credential unable to refresh.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — P1 confidence 75 blocking — Credential-identity collapse: the request carries only user and app while `findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` chooses an arbitrary row, so a user with multiple accounts for one provider has the wrong credential overwritten and the refresh request keyed only by the same user/app pair selects the wrong upstream account.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — P1 confidence 75 blocking — Unversioned last-write-wins transition: the `if (appCredential)` update/create split replaces the entire `key` without a revision, source event ID, or atomic uniqueness invariant, so concurrent first deliveries create competing rows and a delayed retry overwrites a newer refreshed token with stale credentials.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P2 confidence 100 advisory — Cascading-dependency coupling: when the configured sync service is unavailable, the synchronous `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` becomes one shared failure boundary for every expired user-owned Google, HubSpot, Lark, Office 365, Teams, and Webex credential and calendar/video operations fail or continue with stale auth; the strongest counterargument is that the parent service is the authoritative token owner, but the issue survives because one global endpoint couples unrelated providers and provider fallback exists only when configuration is absent rather than when the dependency fails.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — P2 confidence 75 advisory — Stringly integration coupling: the free-form `appSlug: string` is duplicated as hard-coded literals across the Google line 91, HubSpot line 187, Lark line 80, Office calendar line 259, Teams line 73, and Webex line 76 call sites, so an app rename or alias drift silently asks the parent for a different credential; the strongest counterargument is that explicit aliases accommodate provider naming, but the issue survives because webhook creation derives `appMetadata.slug` while refresh has no registry-backed invariant, and the simplification is to delete this parameter and those six literals and derive one canonical ID from the credential/app metadata.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:14 — P2 confidence 100 advisory — Redundant provenance branching: `let refreshTokenResponse` plus the configuration-conditioned branches on lines 15–19 makes validation depend on global deployment state instead of the returned value's declared type, forcing every caller to guess whether it received transport data, parsed data, or a SafeParse envelope; the strongest counterargument is that provider and synchronized responses need different validation, but the issue survives because global state does not identify response origin, and the simplification is to delete lines 14–19 and the wrapper return on line 29 by normalizing the sync transport once in `refreshOAuthTokens` and returning a single typed token DTO.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug. Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 12-18, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is true, it uses minimumTokenResponseSchema which only validates access_token and expiry fields. However, in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, parseRefreshTokenResponse is called with salesforceTokenSchema which includes instance_url, id, signature, scope, token_type. When credential sharing is enabled, the minimumTokenResponseSchema is used instead, which would strip Salesforce-specific fields like instance_url that are needed for the jsforce.Connection to work properly (the connection uses credentialKey.instance_url). This is a real correctness bug where enabling the credential sharing feature breaks Salesforce integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — P1 confidence 75 blocking — Unversioned last-write-wins transition: the `if (appCredential)` update/create split replaces the entire `key` without a revision, source event ID, or atomic uniqueness invariant, so concurrent first deliveries create competing rows and a delayed retry overwrites a newer refreshed token with stale credentials.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in the webhook handler. Looking at lines 56-78 of app-credential.ts, the code does a findFirst to check if credentials exist, then either updates or creates based on that check. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition - between the findFirst and the subsequent create, another concurrent request could create the same credential, leading to duplicate rows. Additionally, the update replaces the entire 'key' field without any versioning or optimistic locking, so a delayed retry with stale credentials could overwrite newer refreshed tokens. The diff shows no unique constraint enforcement or atomic upsert pattern to prevent these issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P2 confidence 100 advisory — Cascading-dependency coupling: when the configured sync service is unavailable, the synchronous `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` becomes one shared failure boundary for every expired user-owned Google, HubSpot, Lark, Office 365, Teams, and Webex credential and calendar/video operations fail or continue with stale auth; the strongest counterargument is that the parent service is the authoritative token owner, but the issue survives because one global endpoint couples unrelated providers and provider fallback exists only when configuration is absent rather than when the dependency fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — P1/100 blocking — Dynamic-key schema failure: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` creates a fixed string-named property rather than accepting arbitrary numeric expiry fields, so Zod strips the sync endpoint's real expiry field and downstream credentials remain expired.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` which evaluates to a literal string key (the string representation of the zod string schema), not a dynamic property matcher. Zod doesn't support dynamic keys this way - this creates a property with a fixed literal key name rather than matching arbitrary numeric expiry fields. This means the schema won't properly validate real expiry fields like 'expires_in' or 'expiry_date', causing the safeParse to potentially fail or strip important fields. The finding correctly identifies this as a schema construction bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — P1/100 blocking — Refresh-token corruption: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` replaces a still-valid stored refresh token with a literal sentinel whenever a valid provider response omits rotation, causing the next direct provider refresh to fail authentication.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts at lines 24-26. The code checks `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token)` and then sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. This is problematic because when a provider doesn't rotate refresh tokens (common behavior), the response won't include a new refresh_token. Setting it to a literal 'refresh_token' string will corrupt the stored credential, and subsequent refresh attempts using this invalid token will fail authentication with the provider. The code should preserve the existing refresh_token from the credential rather than replacing it with a sentinel value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — P1, confidence 100, advisory: works while all future refreshes continue through credential sync, but after `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` overwrites Office 365's real refresh token, disabling or bypassing sync sends the literal placeholder to Microsoft and permanently breaks fallback refresh; although the sync path itself does not consume that token, the failure survives precisely on endpoint outage or configuration rollback when fallback is required.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts at lines 24-26. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and there's no refresh_token in the response, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (a literal placeholder string). This placeholder gets stored in the database via credential.update calls (visible in GoogleCalendarService.ts, Office365CalendarService.ts, etc.). If credential sync is later disabled or fails, the fallback refresh path would use this literal "refresh_token" string instead of a real token, causing permanent authentication failure. The diff shows this exact flow: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns data that gets saved to prisma.credential.update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — P1, confidence 100, blocking: works while Salesforce is fast and available, but `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` runs unconditionally for every service construction with no expiry gate, timeout, or abort signal, so an otherwise valid credential now incurs N redundant refreshes and every request stalls when Salesforce does.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code adds an unconditional fetch to refresh tokens (lines 72-89) that runs every time the service is constructed. Unlike other calendar services in this diff (like GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService) which have a refreshAccessToken function that's called conditionally when tokens expire, the Salesforce implementation performs the refresh immediately in the constructor without any expiry check. This means every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService will make a network request to Salesforce's OAuth endpoint, causing unnecessary API calls and potential latency issues. The finding correctly identifies this as a performance/reliability bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — P2, confidence 100, blocking: invalid ciphertext or decrypted non-JSON reaches `const keys = JSON.parse(` without error mapping, so a malformed credential payload escapes as a raw 500 instead of a 4xx response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 54-56 in app-credential.ts that `symmetricDecrypt` is called followed by `JSON.parse` without any try-catch. If the decryption fails (invalid ciphertext) or the decrypted content is not valid JSON, this will throw an unhandled exception resulting in a 500 error instead of a proper 4xx response with meaningful error message. This is a real defect in error handling for the new webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — P1, confidence 75, blocking: works for serialized deliveries, but when two first-delivery or retry webhooks for the same user/app overlap, `await prisma.credential.findFirst` lets both observe absence before separate creates, yielding duplicate credentials when unconstrained or a raw 500 for one valid delivery when constrained.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in the new webhook handler at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts. The code at lines 57-62 does a findFirst to check if a credential exists, then either updates or creates based on the result. If two concurrent webhook requests for the same user/app arrive simultaneously, both could observe no existing credential and both attempt to create, causing either duplicate records or a database constraint violation. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition that should use upsert or a transaction with proper locking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P1 confidence 100 blocking — `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` sends only enumerable `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` values with no authentication header, so any client that can reach the documented refresh endpoint can impersonate Cal.com and retrieve another user's OAuth access token.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body, with no authentication headers. Looking at the diff, the fetch call at lines 7-14 of refreshOAuthTokens.ts shows no Authorization header or secret being sent. While the receiving endpoint (app-credential.ts) does validate CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET in incoming requests, the outgoing refresh request to the external CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no authentication. This means the external endpoint receiving these requests cannot verify they're from Cal.com, potentially allowing impersonation if that endpoint is reachable.
